best_human.source_location: Östergård (1991), IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 37, 179–180
best_human.provenance: Traditional mixed-code construction reported by the author. The frozen 128-word Hamming-product comparison is a separate, weaker construction.
best_human.reproduction_status: Reported historical construction; identity with the independently verified 2020 OEIS list has not been established.
best_human.ai_provenance: 1991 human publication; no AI role reported

best_public.provenance: Public list credited by OEIS to Dmitry Kamenetsky (2020), verified here as a feasible cover. The exact minimum remains in the interval 107-120.
best_public.evidence_state: all 1024 binary words are covered within Hamming distance 1 by the frozen 120-word list

best_reproduced.provenance: Parsed only the a(10) list from the pinned OEIS A000983 text file; the subsequent a(11) code is excluded.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: benchmark transcription and exact exhaustive verification
best_reproduced.evidence_state: exact bitset check covers all 1024 words

frozen_human_baseline.provenance: Length-7 perfect Hamming code times all 3-bit suffixes.

highest_reported.metric: codewords in a binary length-10 covering code of radius 1
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The 120-word witness is independently verified. Kéri and OEIS record the remaining minimum-size interval as 107-120; no exact optimum claim is made.

optimality_status.evidence_state: OEIS A000983 and the Kéri binary table checked on 2026-11-06 retain 107-120 for length 10, radius 1.

T068-C01.historical_record_note: Östergård (1991) reports a 120-word binary code derived from a 60-word F_4 x F_2^7 mixed code. The public 2020 OEIS word list is treated as a separate frozen witness; no identity between the two is asserted.

reproduced_human_method.source_location: R. W. Hamming, Error Detecting and Error Correcting Codes (1950); binary [7,4,3] Hamming code construction
reproduced_human_method.provenance: Reconstructed as the product of the length-7 perfect Hamming code with all 3-bit suffixes. The parity-check columns are the seven nonzero vectors in F_2^3.
reproduced_human_method.evidence_state: exact parity-check argument and independent full-universe checker confirm coverage
